title: REsilience and Activity every DaY for MS: Pilot Assessment of Efficacy
author: Ambra Mara Giovannetti
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcqjivun

steps.title: Translate and Validate Materials
steps.instruction: Translate the 'READY for MS' therapist and participant manuals, the Drexel Defusion Scale (DDS), and the Comprehensive assessment Acceptance and Commitment Therapy processes (CompACT) into Italian using a three-step validation process.

substeps.instruction: Forward translation: Two qualified translators produce independent translations; a panel (translators, neurologist, psychologist, and lay person) reviews them to reach a consensus version.

Backward translation: A third qualified translator independently translates the consensus version back into English without access to original documents; the backward translation is compared with the original and refined through discussion.

Cognitive debriefing: Administer the Italian DDS and CompACT to 5-10 PwMS of diverse education, age, and EDSS scores, followed by semi-structured interviews to check conceptual equivalence and content validity.

steps.title: Screen and Recruit Participants
steps.instruction: Identify and enroll eligible Multiple Sclerosis (MS) patients based on specific inclusion and exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Verify inclusion criteria: Diagnosis of MS, age >= 18 years, signed informed consent, CDRISC-25 score < 83, ability to attend 7 sessions (2.5 hours each), and fluency in Italian.

Verify exclusion criteria: MMSE < 19, ongoing or recent (within 6 months) psychotherapy, previous experience in meditation/mind-body therapies, major psychiatric disorders, pregnancy, MS diagnosis < 3 months, or one or more relapses in the last month.

steps.title: Perform Baseline Evaluation (T0)
steps.instruction: Conduct the initial assessment of all eligible participants before group allocation.

substeps.instruction: Administer PROMs in order: MSQOL-54, CDRISC-25, HADS, PSS, CompACT, MAAS, VLQ, AAQII, and DDS.
Administer the SEIQoL-DW interview.
Collect clinical data from the neurologist: EDSS score, MS course, co-pathologies, and ongoing treatment.

steps.title: Randomize Participants
steps.instruction: Assign participants to either the 'READY for MS' group or the relaxation control group in a 1:1 ratio using computer-based block randomization.

substeps.instruction: Use two block factors: EDSS score (< 2.0 and >= 2.0) and CDRISC-25 score (< 50 and >= 50).

steps.title: Implement READY for MS Intervention
steps.instruction: Deliver a 7-module resilience training program based on ACT, consisting of weekly 2.5-hour group sessions guided by a trained psychotherapist.

substeps.instruction: Session 1 (Introduction): Build rapport, outline program structure/READY personal plan, and educate on protective factors and early warning signs of low resilience.
Session 2 (Mindfulness): Review previous session, introduce mindfulness, and practice exercises (eating a sultana, sound, sight, breathing, and physical sensations). Assign home exercises.
Session 3 (Defusion I): Practice mindfulness, educate on thought fusion vs. defusion, identify unhelpful thoughts, and practice defusion strategies. Assign home exercises.
Session 4 (Defusion II and Observer Self): Troubleshoot defusion strategies, introduce the 'Observer Self' vs. 'Conceptualised Self', and reflect on personal stories related to MS.
Session 5 (Acceptance): Educate on emotion management and experiential avoidance; practice acceptance strategies (e.g., 'Stop; Notice; Let go; Make space').
Session 6 (Values and Meaningful Action): Develop value statements, identify meaningful actions consistent with values, and explore social connectedness and self-care strategies.
Session 7 (Finale): Synthesize key learnings, map resilience strategies to protective factors, and refine the personal plan to address early warning signs.

steps.title: Implement Control Relaxation Program
steps.instruction: Deliver a group relaxation program consisting of 7 weekly one-hour group sessions to control for non-specific effects.

steps.title: Conduct Booster Session
steps.instruction: Administer a 2.5-hour booster session approximately 5 weeks after the final intervention session.

substeps.instruction: Begin with a mindfulness exercise.
Review READY program contents and discuss participants' progress in applying learned strategies.

steps.title: Perform Follow-up Assessments
steps.instruction: Collect data at specified time points to evaluate efficacy.

substeps.instruction: T1 (7 weeks after baseline): Administer MSQOL-54, CDRISC-25, HADS, PSS, CompACT, MAAS, VLQ, AAQII, and DDS. Neurologist updates EDSS, treatment, and relapses.
T2 (12 weeks after baseline): Administer all T1 PROMs plus SEIQoL-DW. Neurologist updates EDSS, treatment, and relapses.
T3 (24 weeks after baseline): Administer all T1 PROMs plus SEIQoL-DW.

steps.title: Conduct Qualitative Interviews
steps.instruction: Perform semi-structured personal interviews with approximately 50% of the 'READY for MS' group within 3 months of treatment completion.

substeps.instruction: Use an interview guide with open-ended questions regarding resilience, changes in thinking/feeling, helpful skills, and program strengths/weaknesses.
Audio-record and transcribe interviews verbatim for thematic analysis.
